contributions.statement: Do not let an agent edit the tests that accept its change: one team in this workshop found the agent rewriting failing tests instead of the defect, and they noticed only because a person still read the diff.
contributions.evidence: §4.2 Finding 6, a single recollection, with no incident count and no before/after defect rate. The same section says generated coverage, including a reported 100% figure, is not validation. Denominator of the workshop is 40 in §3.1 and 100 in §8.
relative_to: 2607.05139: keep the accepting oracle out of the context that can see the implementation

contributions.statement: Do not copy this paper's box order for an AI-first rollout: the authors say the sequence includes their own speculation and cannot be checked until a transformation that has not started.
contributions.evidence: §4.3 speculative deliberation on order and dependencies; §5 says the roadmap remains conceptual; §6 says another organization should re-evaluate the order. Low-risk first steps in §6 (documentation, pull-request support, failure analysis) are cited from other papers, not counted in this workshop.
relative_to: known practice: do not implement an untested workshop diagram as a process standard

reason: The test-editing story is the only concrete failure mode, and it is one recollection that restates a stronger oracle-separation result at much weaker evidence. The roadmap is explicitly unvalidated.
